track.name: Entre dos fuegos
track.comment: First recording with the new orchestra

track.name: Fuegos artificiales
track.comment: Only known studio recording by D'Arienzo. Another version was recorded for the radio show "Ronda Musical de las Américas", ca. 1946

track.name: Candombe oriental
track.author: Pintín Castellanos
track.comment: The CD El Bandoneón n°109, "Cambalache" mentions, erroneously, Alberto Echagüe, who had already left in 1941 and would only return in 1944.

track.name: Dime, mi amor
track.author: Manuel Romero
track.comment: With this theme D'Arienzo participates in the movie "Yo Quiero Ser Bataclana" (Manuel Romero, 1941) this time a duo with with Juan Carlos Thorry and Sabina Olmos (see the fragment on Youtube). In the same movie D'Arienzo interprets El Vino Tristo (with Nini Marshall) and also directs, in the train scene (foto), Yo Quiero Ser Bataclana (no known studio recording)

track.name: El rey del compás
track.comment: Tango dedicated to D'Arienzo, first recorded by the Orq. Típica Víctor (1939).

track.name: Embrujamiento
track.author: Manuel Enrique Ferradás Campos
track.comment: The same composition, but with the original title "Metido", was recorded by Fresedo (with Roberto Ray, 1932) and Biagi (with Alberto Lago, 1942). Possibly another case of title change in tango due to radio censorship in 1943 (aimed at banning all popular and Lunfardo expressions)

track.name: El lazo
track.author: Eugenio Cardenas
track.comment: At the end of 1942, Víctor changed its record numbering system (from the 3xxxx series to the 60-xxxx series). We now see clearly that this recording was published at least 2 months after its production. The strict rhythm of the early years (2 recorded - 2 published, and so on...) gradually eroded from the end of 1941 on, by mixing recordings of different sessions on a single edition.

track.name: Se fue
track.author: P. Valdez
track.comment: Baba mentions 3 authors: Oscar Rubens and P. Valdez (pseudonym) are in fact the same person.

track.name: El huracán
track.author: Nolo López
track.comment: Only known recording by D'Arienzo. The one that appears on the Lantower CD "Juan D'Arienzo y su Orquesta, Vol.1" (n°5 in the "Grandes del Tango" series) is in fact the recording by Carlos Lazzari y su Orq. Juan D'Arienzo from 1987.

track.name: Sigueme, si puedes
track.author: Antonio Anselmi
track.comment: Original title: Seguime Si Podés, as used by all others (Canaro, 1928 - Juan Sanchez Gorio, 1952 - Osvaldo Pugliese, 1953 ...). Once again related to the puritanism of the radio censorship years (1943-1949) ?

track.name: Me duele el corazón
track.composer: arr. O. Maderna, C. Yeguit, Luis Mendoza
track.author: C. Yeguit, Luis Mendoza

track.name: Don Alfonso
track.comment: With this theme, D'Arienzo participates in the movie "El Cantor del Pueblo" (1948).

track.name: Siempre amigos
track.author: Enrique Cadícamo
track.comment: This title may cause some confusion. "Siempre Amigos" is the title of a tango by Benjamin Tagle Lara with lyrics by Carlos V.G. Flores (which has been recorded by Ignacio Corsini). However, the one mentioned here, is better known as "Pa'mi es igual (Siempre amigos)". Although I have never seen the original disco all sources seem to mention "Siempre amigos", in fact the subtitle.

track.name: Se apagó una estrella
track.composer: Emilio Pellejero, Guillermo Yorio, José Santanero
track.author: Emilio Pellejero, Guillermo Yorio, José Santanero

track.name: Muchachita del recuerdo
track.composer: Cayetano Puglisi, Ernesto de la Cruz
track.author: Carlos Marín

track.name: As de bastos (Rey de triunfo)
track.comment: The same recording (master number 91470) was reedited on record 68-0223 (same contents as 60-1875) but with the alternate title "Rey de Triunfo" Even record nr. 60-1875 itself was edited with both titles !

track.comment: See also the note at the 1941 version

track.author: José Rótulo
track.comment: Original title: Nací en Pompeya (as it is registered at SADAIC)
